podcast.title: Bear Logo Acceptance and Evolution
podcast.body: Tom Yorke confirmed in an interview that he initially admired the macabre image of the bear and used it exclusively for "Kid A" (QD) advertising. The bear's widespread acceptance by the public ultimately led to its adoption as one of Radiohead's standard logos, despite not being initially conceived as such. "Tom Yorke hacía referencia de que le había gustado un montón, esa imagen macabra de losos que la usó solo como publicidad para el QD. Pero luego le acabó gustando un montón, tuvo un montón de aceptación y que finalmente se quedó como uno de los logán se está en der de la banda."

podcast.title: Cyclical Creative Process
podcast.body: Tom Yorke is characterized by a distinctive creative pattern, marked by alternating phases of intense creative explosion and profound creative crisis or depression. The "Kid A" sessions, for example, represent the zenith of his creative output during such an explosive phase. "Tom George es una persona que combina enormes fases de explosión creativa con enormes fases de crisis creativa y de depresión."

podcast.title: Dr. Shock Alias
podcast.body: Tom Yorke used the pseudonym Dr. Shock for artistic expression projects that were not musical in nature. Under this alias, he signed various paintings and collaborated with Stanley Donwood on visual arts, including projections and the comic that inspired the Radiohead bear logo. "Dr. Shock realmente es el seudónimo con el que Tom York hacía ciertos trabajos de expresión artística que no era musical. Es el nombre como el que firmó algunos cuadros, incluso trabajos con Stan Lee Donwood sobre artes, sobre proyectiones y estas cosas."

podcast.title: Interest in Electronic Music and Technology
podcast.body: Tom Yorke developed a keen interest in electronics, exploring various new music systems. He learned from other electronic artists and became proficient in using sampling machines and recording canned sounds. These new interests and acquired skills became fundamental to the future direction and sound of Radiohead. "Él se ha interesado mucho por la electrónica, conocía muchos otras artistas electrónicos que le habían enseñado muchos sistemas de música nuevos, él aprendió a utilizar muchísimas máquinas desampleados, agravar sonidos en latados."

podcast.title: NME Interview on Kid A Material
podcast.body: In an interview with NME, Tom Yorke expressed the overwhelming volume of material generated during the "Kid A" sessions. He famously stated that he wished he could have released ten albums from the content produced during that period, indicating the difficulty he faced in selecting what to include. "En una entrevista a enemy Tom George llegó a decir que le hubiese gustado sacar 10 agúmes puntos con esa gollquidad porque realmente llevo un punto en que él no sabía que renunciar."

podcast.title: Pre-Kid A Creative Explosion Assessment
podcast.body: Tom Yorke characterized the period immediately preceding the release of "Kid A" as the band's most significant explosion of artistic creativity. During this time, the band produced a wealth of music alongside numerous other projects, such as posters, short films, videos, animations, and comics. "la mayor explosión de creatividad artística de la banda, como siempre ha referido a Tom York a ese periodo del que no solo salió muchísima música sino que salieron un montón de otros proyectos."
